gaps.term: why the two outer updates are linear-time while the middle one is costly
gaps.quote: Both change only $D$, each combining $D$ with the earlier field $H$ in linear time.
gaps.note: The page asserts that D <- D-H and D <- H-D cost linear time on the tapes while H <- H+D is 'the costly one', giving only that H is 'the earlier field' (an ordering of the fields never set up on the page). The reader, who has not studied tape-level data movement, cannot check why updating D from H is a linear-time rearrangement while updating H from D is not.
